name: Stortok
description: Stortok (Swedish: 'Big Fool') is a Swedish card game related to the Russian game Durak. The primary goal is to get rid of all your cards. The winner is the first player out, and the last player holding cards is the 'Stortok' (Fool). It features attacking and defending mechanics, but with fewer complex card interactions than Durak.
deck: Standard 36-card deck (A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6 - remove 2, 3, 4, 5).

The winner is the first player out, and the last player holding cards is the 'Stortok' (Fool). It features attacking and defending mechanics, but with fewer complex card interactions than Durak.

history.origins: Stortok is known from three documented sources: Lindskog (1847), Öberg (1858), and Schenkmanis (1980s, also in Norwegian as Kjempetosk). It is a Swedish beating game related to Durak, with two trump suits (high and low by colour). The 1847 and 1858 accounts differ from the late 20th-century version in deal size, trick structure, and lead rules.
timeline: 1970s: Included in Swedish card game books.
history.evolution: The rules are simpler than Durak (e.g., usually specific attackers or anyone attacks).

setup.players: Two to five players. The game is for 2 to 5 players; deal and play are clockwise.
setup.deck: 36-card pack: from a standard 52-card pack remove the cards below 6; ranks A (high) down to 6 (low) in each suit.
setup.dealing: Deal 5 cards to each player. Top card of remaining deck turned for Trump. Remainder forms Talon.

rules.objective: To get rid of all one's cards. The last player left with cards is the loser and is called the Great Fool (Stortok).
rules.gameplay: Forehand (left of dealer) leads any card to start the play pile. Each player in turn must beat the top card (same suit higher, or any trump on non-trump, or high trump on low trump) or pick up the whole play pile. When everyone has beaten, the trick is complete and the last player to play leads the next. When a player picks up, the player to their right (who played the highest card in the incomplete trick) leads. So long as the stock has cards, after each card played the player draws one from the stock. When the stock is exhausted, play continues until one player remains with cards; that player is the Stortok (loser).
keyRules: Same suit: higher rank beats. Non-trump beaten by any low or high trump. Low trump beaten by any high trump.
Pick up the whole play pile if unable or unwilling to beat the top card.
Draw one from stock after each play while stock has cards.
Last player with cards is the Stortok (Great Fool).

strategy.basic: Save high trumps for defense. Don't waste them on low non-trumps unless necessary. Try to attack with pairs if allowed (to force defender to use two good cards).
strategy.intermediate: Hand Management: Keep a variety of suits to avoid being forced to trump unnecessarily.
strategy.advanced: Card Counting: Remember which trumps have been played. If the Ace of Trumps is gone, the King is boss.
tips: The goal is not to win tricks, but to shed.
Attacking drains your hand, which is good.

variations.name: 1847 (Lindskog)
variations.description: 36 cards, 5 each, stock with turned trump; two trump suits (high and low by colour). Play pile; beat or pick up; draw after each play while stock has cards.

variations.name: 1858 (Öberg)
variations.description: Full 52-card deck; all cards dealt; last card dealt face up determines high trump. No stock; play continues until one player has all cards (the Stortok).
